theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.kind: adversarial finding about THIS REPO, found because the change sprang it. Not a defect in P-259b's code; a defect in the terrain that any column-adding lane will hit.
theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.whatHappened: `lib/db` keeps a frozen `pg_dump` of the public schema at lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template. `@workspace/db/testing`'s `withTestSchema` does NOT read the drizzle schema: it replays that template into a fresh `test_<ts>_<rand>` schema. So the moment `txgio_parcel`'s drizzle declaration gained `zoning_district_interim`, every integration test that writes the table failed with `error: column "zoning_district_interim" of relation "txgio_parcel" does not exist` (SQLSTATE 42703) -- measured, 9 tests.
theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.whyItWouldHaveFailedCi: pr-checks.yml's Test job runs a pgvector/pgvector:pg14 service, `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run push` (drizzle-kit push, which reads the drizzle schema and therefore DOES create the column), then `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run test:fixture:drift`, then `pnpm test`. The drift check pg_dumps the pushed live schema and diffs it against the committed template, so a column added to the schema without refreshing the template fails the pull request on drift -- and the integration harness fails separately, because it replays the stale template rather than the pushed schema.
theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.theFix: one line in the template, beside its neighbours (`zoning_district_interim boolean` after `zoning_jurisdiction`, matching the drizzle schema's own field order): lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template. This is the same maintenance the two previous columns on this table needed -- `zoning_jurisdiction` (migration 0062) and its predecessors are already in the template.
theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.verificationIsNotAJudgementCall: a throwaway pgvector/pgvector:pg14 container, postgis + vector extensions, `drizzle-kit push`, then `pg_dump --schema-only --no-owner --no-acl --no-comments --schema=public` piped through the drift script's OWN filter/sed pipeline (reproduced in node, since this box has no bash+pg_dump): `committed template: 5172 lines / live dump (filtered): 5172 lines / NOTHING TO DO: Schema fixture matches live DB.` ZERO drift, line for line.
theSchemaFixtureDriftTrap.consequenceForTheClose: this is why the diff carries an 11th file that the dispatch never names. It is not scope creep: without it the pull request's own Test check fails, and the failure would look like a zoning bug.

theStagingIncident.kind: an incident CAUSED BY THIS LANE. Disclosed at the same volume as the findings.
theStagingIncident.whatHappened: the three dry-run legs need DATABASE_URL, so the staging DSN was exported into this shell session. It stayed exported. A later `npx vitest run` over lib/cad-ingest therefore satisfied `hasDb` in src/__tests__/txgioIngest.integration.test.ts, which took the `@workspace/db` `withTestSchema` branch -- a harness that CREATEs and DROPs a `test_<ts>_<rand>` schema in whatever database DATABASE_URL names. That test file's own header says, in capitals: 'NEVER point DATABASE_URL at a deployment database to run this: the harness creates and drops schemas.' It was pointed at LDT STAGING. 9 tests then failed on the missing column (the trap above), i.e. they failed on their FIRST insert, before writing a row.
theStagingIncident.blastRadiusMeasuredNotAssumed: read-only probe against the same store afterwards (_scratch/p259b-staging-integrity.mjs in the doc worktree): (a) `SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname ~ '^test_[0-9]+_'` returns ZERO rows -- `withTestSchema` drops in a `finally`, so no schema survived; (b) `public.txgio_parcel` row counts are 131,734 (48209) / 304,298 (48491) / 894,657 (48453) -- IDENTICAL to the predecessor's independently measured figures, so no row was added or removed; (c) 0 rows were written because every failing statement was an INSERT that errored as a unit.
theStagingIncident.whatWasStillConsumed: the staging database's DDL path was exercised nine times (schema create + full template replay + drop) on a shared store. That is churn no lane is entitled to cause on a deployment database, and no data change does not make it nothing.
theStagingIncident.theCorrection: every subsequent DB-touching run was against a THROWAWAY local pgvector/pgvector:pg14 container (the image and extension steps CI uses), with DATABASE_URL pointing at localhost. The full cad-ingest suite and the lib/db suite were both re-run there.
theStagingIncident.theLessonWorthKeeping: exporting DATABASE_URL for one command silently ARMS every integration test in the repo, and the arming is invisible: the tests report as skipped when it is unset and as failures when it is set to a deployment store. `TEST_DATABASE_URL` exists as the separate variable for exactly this reason -- the fix for a future lane is to export TEST_DATABASE_URL (which the harness prefers) and never DATABASE_URL, or to point DATABASE_URL at a container.

adversarialNotes: A GREEN SUITE IS NOT THE GRADE, and here the suite was not green either. The most valuable thing this checkpoint found was not a zoning behaviour: it was that the repo's integration harness mirrors a hand-refreshed pg_dump, so adding a column silently invalidates every write-path test in the repo until the template is refreshed. That is a trap for the NEXT column-adding lane, and it is worth more than the column.

THE FALSIFIER THAT COULD HAVE FLATTERED US. Falsifier 4's sentence is not literally true -- 'stamped rows == account-bearing features' cannot hold in a county that is mostly outside the city. The temptation was to report the identity that DOES hold (buckets sum to features read) and call the sentence PASS. Instead the shortfall is printed: 173,111 Travis account-bearing features are in no Austin polygon, and the sentence's first half is recorded FALSE-AS-WRITTEN with its counterexample. The decomposition that CP1 pre-registered is what was graded.

THE SKIP HAS A COST AND IT IS MEASURED, not buried: 23,886 fewer rows on Travis than the predecessor's run (21,573 formerly matched + 2,313 formerly planned-development). The no-account features were not previously null-only; a fifth of them were being stamped. Any share computed from a previous run's matched count is now comparing a different population.

THE DISCLOSURE IS A ROW FACT, NOT A LOG FACT: writing `interim` only into the CLI's output would leave it unrecoverable from the store, which does not satisfy 'the stamped row records that the district is interim'. The column is the decision; the log is the second copy. Its semantics are three-valued on purpose -- NULL means nothing was stamped, so a NULL can never be read as an understated 'not interim'.

THE PREREQUISITE IS DECLARED, NOT ASSUMED: the stamp's write names `zoning_district_interim` on every row, so on a database without migration 0103 Postgres rejects the UPDATE (42703) and the first batch aborts with zero rows written. That is fail-closed and it was OBSERVED (the integration tests hit exactly that error against staging). The integration seat must apply 0103 before `--apply`, the same prerequisite shape migration 0059 documented for `zoning_district`.

THE SCHEMA FIXTURE IS A REVIEWABLE ARTEFACT, NOT A SMOKE TEST: the template line was verified by reproducing the drift script's own pipeline against a pushed CI-shaped database, not by eyeballing the file. Zero drift, 5172 lines against 5172.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: lib/db's integration harness (`@workspace/db/testing` -> `withTestSchema`) replays a hand-refreshed `pg_dump` Fixture (lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template) into its disposable schema -- it does NOT read the drizzle schema. So adding a column to any drizzle table silently breaks every write-path integration test with SQLSTATE 42703 until the template is refreshed, and CI fails the PR twice over (the drift check compares a pushed live DB against the template). Refresh it in the same change: `pnpm --filter @workspace/db run test:fixture:schema`, or hand-add the line beside its neighbours as this lane did.

Exporting DATABASE_URL arms every integration test in the repo, invisibly (they SKIP when it is unset and RUN when it is set). A `*>`-redirected dry run and a `npx vitest run` in the same shell session means the test suite inherits your deployment DSN and `withTestSchema` CREATEs and DROPs schemas in it. Use TEST_DATABASE_URL (the harness prefers it) or point DATABASE_URL at a throwaway container.

node on this Windows box cannot verify Google Frontend's TLS chain with its bundled CA store: `fetch` fails `unable to verify the first certificate` / UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE. The lease script reports it as `{"code":"FAILED","message":"fetch failed"}`, which reads like a credentials problem and is not one. Run node with `--use-system-ca` (or NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca) for the lease script AND for any ArcGIS fetch. Symptom in the stamp CLI: `layer metadata: UNAVAILABLE (the host did not answer ?f=json)` immediately followed by `FATAL: TypeError: fetch failed`.

The heavy-scan lease API lives in project hauska-prod-497015 (Cloud Run service `factory-control`, region us-east4, https://factory-control-h7gvu7rgcq-uk.a.run.app) with its key in Secret Manager `FACTORY_CONTROL_API_KEY` there. It is NOT in legacy-design-tools-prod, which only holds FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO. Endpoint paths: GET /heavy-scan-leases[?store=], GET /heavy-scan-lease?holderToken=, POST /heavy-scan-lease-{take,renew,release}; every mutation needs the `x-factory-operator` header or it is refused as a sentinel.
